Problem: Any logged-in user can change any user's password by id.

Problem: Any logged-in user can add, edit or delete permissions.

Problem: Totals, prices and discounts come from the browser and are saved as sent. A tampered request can create any amount.

Problem: Endpoints accept any role id (also Super-admin) and any user id (also the Admin). The form only hides them.

Problem: Un-defaulting or deleting the default GST leaves no default, so new invoices get 0 tax.

Problem: Saving the default GST without ticking "default" silently un-defaults it.

Problem: Root cause found. The button links to invoice/edit/{id}. InvoiceController@edit (line ~684) and @update (line ~1044) both start with $this->invoicesVisibleToCurrentUser(), and that helper (line 47) begins with Appointment::where('is_invoiced', 1). A booked appointment has is_invoiced = NULL, so ->firstOrFail() throws and the browser shows 404. (For staff the helper also keeps only rows where invoice_created_by is the staff, which a booking never has.) The page itself and update() are fine: update() already turns the row into an invoice (status = 1, is_invoiced = 1, new invoice number).
Suggested fix: Add a second helper for these two actions and use it in edit() and update() (keep invoicesVisibleToCurrentUser() for the invoice list): private function appointmentForInvoicing($id) { $q = Appointment::where('appointment_id', $id)->where(fn($q) => $q->where('is_invoiced', 1)->orWhereIn('status', [0, 3, 4])); $u = auth()->user(); if ($u && $u->isStaffUser() && !$u->can('Pos_invoice-Show_All')) { $q->where(fn($q) => $q->where('invoice_created_by', $u->getKey())->orWhereHas('services', fn($s) => $s->where('staff_id', $u->getKey()))); } return $q; } Then $appointment = $this->appointmentForInvoicing($id)->firstOrFail(); in edit($id) and $this->appointmentForInvoicing($request->input('appointment_id'))->firstOrFail(); in update(). In update() also add 'invoice_created_by' => $appointment->invoice_created_by ?? auth()->id() to the $appointment->update([...]) array, otherwise staff cannot open the invoice they just made.

Problem: The calendar only has a column for staff with is_barber = 1. A booking created for any other staff (for example JOJO, Jack Sparrow in the local DB) is invisible in the calendar. Calendar create does not check is_barber.

Problem: Overlap check compares TIME columns with full datetimes, is inclusive (an appointment starting exactly when another ends is refused) and ignores status (a cancelled appointment still blocks the slot).

Problem: The invoice email is sent inside the DB transaction; if mail fails the invoice is rolled back.

Problem: Duplicate phone numbers allowed; booking uses the first match; POS can create a duplicate.

Problem: Stored with users.role = 'Staff', so a Manager is scoped like staff and blocked from reports.

Problem: New barber's default hours (09:00-13:00, 14:00-18:00) are saved as break_type = 2 (a break), but "My working hours" reads break_type = 1, so new staff start with an empty hours page.

Problem: Revenue / appointments / visits are for the whole shop, only tips and commission are the person's own; the staff's total product commission is repeated on every day row.
Suggested fix: Scope every card to the staff, show the product commission per day.

Problem: "Total spend" adds each invoice once per service line, plus every product commission ever generated.
Suggested fix: Sum each invoice once.

Problem: Re-prices every line at today's catalog price, rewriting history.
Suggested fix: Keep the stored price of unchanged lines.

Problem: The tip split is stored as unrounded floats (1.6666666667).
Suggested fix: Split in cents so the parts add up.

Problem: The row query ignores the end date (start date is written twice); the summary honours both.
Suggested fix: Apply both dates in the main query.

Problem: "Amount" is what the staff earned (commission + tips), not the invoice total.
Suggested fix: Rename the column or show the invoice total.

Problem: Top products grouped by product and discount (several rows per product); appointments report rows need an invoiced appointment but its summary only needs status 1; payments report ignores the staff filter.
Suggested fix: Make rows and summaries use the same rules; honour the filter.

Problem: "Replace image" writes a description column that does not exist (SQL error). Gallery routes have no permission check (only the buttons are hidden).

Problem: A missing active_status checkbox silently sets status 0.

Problem: Product stock never decreases when a product is sold.
Suggested fix: Decrement stock on sale (and restore on edit / delete).

Problem: Returns every appointment ever and every break, no date range.
Suggested fix: Require start / end.

Problem: Rows found by day name only; a staff row can be overwritten if it sorts first.

Problem: The customer record is found by phone and not renamed when the name changes.
Suggested fix: Update the customer name too, or tell the user.

Problem: A deleted method's name stays reserved (the unique rule counts deleted rows).
Suggested fix: Ignore soft-deleted rows in the unique rule.

Problem: A service booked with quantity 2 is checked as one unit.
Suggested fix: Use the real quantity.

Problem: Ignores the barber's active_status.

Problem: Placeholder email / phone of another brand (info@bluecrownbarbers.com, (555) 123-4567).
Suggested fix: Use Rosenthal's or leave blank.

Problem: Staff dashboard counts "first available" lines for the staff, the staff list excludes them; "today" excludes invoiced appointments.
Suggested fix: Make both screens use one rule.

Problem: Laravel uses America/Edmonton but MySQL NOW() uses the server clock (about 6 h different). Raw NOW() mixes the two.

Problem: A search that matches through a staff name shows only that staff member's lines in the row.
Suggested fix: Search without filtering the joined rows.

Problem: The POS lists inactive services/products too.

Where: Staff > a staff member > Earnings tab
Problem: Staff > a staff member > Earnings tab: the same product commission on every day row. StaffController.php lines ~123-154: $productSub is grouped by staff_id only (the staff's whole product commission) and joined to the daily rows with s.staff_id = p.staff_id, then the rows are grouped by a.date, s.staff_id, p.product_commission. So every day shows the staff's total, and total_earn per day is inflated by it. Proof (staff 49, six day rows): the table shows $63.85 on every row; the real product commission per day is 4.60, 1.70, 0.00, 3.30, 0.00, 1.00 (sum 63.85). The summary cards above the table are correct. Fix: group $productSub by appointment_id, staff_id, join it on a.appointment_id = p.appointment_id AND p.staff_id = s.staff_id, and use SUM(p.product_commission) per date.

Where: Q68 Staff money: commission audit (checked against the local database, 2026-11-04)
Problem: SUM(DISTINCT ...) on commission and tip (Reports > Staff tab, the barber's own Staff Report, dashboard Top Services). It adds each *different amount* once, so every repeated amount (most services have a fixed price, so most commissions repeat) disappears. Measured for staff 49, October 2026, 150 invoices: real service commission $1,336.28, SUM(DISTINCT) gives $284.13 (under-reported by about 79%). Same issue for tips and for SUM(DISTINCT total_amt) revenue. Fix: sum per appointment without DISTINCT (the join is already one row per appointment and staff, so a plain SUM is right); keep COUNT(DISTINCT appointment_id) for counts. This is Q1/Q36 with real numbers: please treat it as the top priority, the owner uses these figures to pay staff.
